page: Microsoft Azure E2ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Configured on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core across two threads. The system includes 16.0 GB of memory, achieving a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per virtual CPU, along with 32 MB of shared L3 cache and support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, SHA-NI, and VAES. Local high-speed ephemeral storage is bundled via a 118 GB NVMe SSD, while no discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are present.

Benchmark testing reflects the constraints of its two-vCPU hardware footprint alongside robust single-threaded efficiency. Single-core evaluations are strong, with Geekbench achieving 1966.0 and stress-ng reaching 3076.88, both landing in the top 25% of evaluated systems. Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded metrics remain low due to the single physical core layout, visible in a PassMark CPU score of 3831.31 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2435.0. Memory throughput displays average write speeds of 27.74 GB/sec on large uncached blocks, while Redis reaches 2.95 million SET operations per second.

From a qualitative cost and infrastructure perspective, the E2ads_v6 provides an accessible entry point to AMD-based memory-heavy configurations. It delivers substantial RAM capacity and fast local NVMe storage without requiring large core allocations. However, applications bound by heavy multi-threaded compute, high-throughput caching engines, or dense database transactional processing may encounter throughput bottlenecks given the two-thread CPU ceiling. The instance is primarily suited for memory-sensitive lightweight workloads, including small in-memory caches, development environments, low-traffic enterprise services, and background batch jobs.
